A1.justification: Both complete 24-page PDFs describe the same ADAlign research, including Appendices A–E. Text and rendered pages 2–24 are identical; the first-page differences are limited to punctuation, spacing, and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original ADAlign experiments, including node classification across 10 datasets and 16 transfer scenarios, efficiency measurements, and ablations.

after.justification: The same original classification, efficiency, and supplementary experimental results remain in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same neural spectral discrepancy, amplitude–phase alignment, adaptive frequency sampler, and minimax training procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 16 transfer scenarios across the ArnetMiner, Airport, Blog, and Twitch datasets. Section 5.1 and Appendix D.1 contain identical coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the main classification tables, efficiency comparison, backbone experiments, and embedding visualization. No evaluated baseline is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, training settings, hyperparameter searches, and experimental procedures are unchanged in Section 5, Appendix D.3, and Table 7.

E4.justification: The frequency-sampler ablations, parameter sensitivity studies, backbone comparisons, training curves, embedding visualizations, and learned-frequency analyses are identical, including Appendix E.

E5.justification: Both disclose five-run averaging in Appendix D.3, report scores with ±σ, and present the same paired two-sided t-tests in Appendix E.2.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, ADAlign's A→C Micro-F1 remains 82.21±0.36 in Table 1; the efficiency and appendix results also match exactly.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, discrepancy derivations, generalization bound, and propositions are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same assumptions and proof, and Appendix C.1 retains the same complexity analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical scientific claims about adaptive spectral alignment, classification performance, training stability, and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of spectral components, efficiency, stability, parameter sensitivity, and embedding quality are unchanged. No substantive applicability qualification or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Training documentation, hyperparameters, hardware, software versions, and implementation details remain identical. The code URL and its hyperlink target are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and the positioning against prior graph adaptation and characteristic-function research are identical.

P1.justification: v2 removes a standalone extra period below the abstract's code-availability sentence and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first page has slight vertical spacing adjustments around the abstract and introduction. All figures, tables, captions, and layouts on pages 2–24 are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 makes a cosmetic punctuation and spacing correction on the first page. The scientific content, evidence, theoretical arguments, and reproducibility information—including all appendices—remain identical, so the cleanup does not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
